An exception to this rule is if you are purposefully relying on the cache engine to manage your keys by means of eviction, also referred to as an LRU cache."

Using this feature, you can create cross-Region read replica clusters for ElastiCache to enable low-latency reads and disaster recovery across AWS Regions."

### elasticache-read-replicas-eventual-consistency-tolerant-workloads

**Claim.** Session stores, leaderboards and recommendation engines handle many more reads than writes and can often tolerate slightly stale data (eventual consistency), so read replicas are an effective way to reduce read latency.

**Write it as.** `session stores, leaderboards, and recommendation engines` · `can often tolerate slightly stale data (eventual consistency)`

**Scope.** ElastiCache read replicas.

> "Many applications, such as session stores, leaderboards, and recommendation engines, require high availability and handle significantly more read operations than write operations. These applications can often tolerate slightly stale data (eventual consistency), meaning that it's acceptable if different users momentarily see slightly different versions of the same data."
> — [Best Practices for using Read Replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/ReadReplicas.html)

> "Eventual consistency means that all replica nodes will eventually return the same data once the replication process is complete, typically within milliseconds. For such use cases, implementing read replicas is an effective strategy to reduce latency when reading from your ElastiCache instance."
> — [Best Practices for using Read Replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/ReadReplicas.html)

### elasticache-without-multi-az-new-primary-provisioned-longer-interruption

**Claim.** If Multi-AZ is not enabled and a primary node fails, ElastiCache takes the primary offline and provisions a new primary node. It syncs from a replica if one exists; otherwise it starts empty and data is lost unless you restore from a snapshot. The write interruption is longer than with automatic failover. The same page notes one exception: automatic failover can be enabled without Multi-AZ; failover then still promotes a replica to primary if one is available, but replicas are not guaranteed to be in different Availability Zones, so this does not protect against AZ-level failures.

**Write it as.** `provisions a new primary node` · `starts empty and data is lost`

**Scope.** Valkey and Redis OSS replication groups; Multi-AZ not enabled; automatic failover enabled without Multi-AZ is the stated exception.

> "If Multi-AZ is not enabled and a primary node fails, ElastiCache takes the primary offline and provisions a new primary node. If replicas exist, ElastiCache syncs the new primary from a replica. If no replicas exist, the new primary starts empty and data is lost unless you restore from a snapshot. This process results in a longer write interruption compared to automatic failover."
> — [Minimizing downtime in ElastiCache by using Multi-AZ with Valkey and Redis OSS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/AutoFailover.html)

> "While it is possible to have automatic failover enabled without Multi-AZ, replicas are not guaranteed to be in different Availability Zones in this configuration. Failover still promotes a replica to primary if one is available, but this does not protect against AZ-level failures."
> — [Minimizing downtime in ElastiCache by using Multi-AZ with Valkey and Redis OSS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/AutoFailover.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-14.
